title: Entropically smoothed worst-training-group risk
formal_object: Training-source groups g=1..G with means L_g(w), G>=2, fixed gamma>0; F(w)=gamma log sum_g exp(L_g(w)/gamma).
assumptions: Groups are declared by training provenance, not test outcomes; each has positive sample count.
All group losses use the same units and fixed gamma. Smooth worst-training-group loss is not worst-test-task generalization.
Finite gradient descent with ridge is an approximate optimization, not Sagawa's persistent online group adversary.

derivation_steps.statement: Stationarity of sum a_g L_g-gamma sum a_g log a_g gives a_g=exp(L_g/gamma)/Z.
derivation_steps.justification: Normalization follows the simplex multiplier; strict entropy concavity gives the unique optimum.

derivation_steps.statement: max L_g <= F <= max L_g+gamma log G.
derivation_steps.justification: Factor out exp(max L/gamma); remaining positive sum is in [1,G].

derivation_steps.statement: grad F=sum a_g grad L_g, with group means dividing by n_g.
derivation_steps.justification: Differentiate log partition, including the dependence of L_g on w; this is not an arbitrary detached adaptive weighting.

method_expression: Use the explicit F plus the same anchored ridge as ERM, preserve all per-group training losses and full native task outputs; audit finite solver cost. Do not substitute this objective for the author group-DRO online update.
distinguishing_prediction: Benefits, if any, should track changes in observed group loss dispersion and transfer to predeclared test tasks; small gamma increases emphasis on the current hard training group.
falsifier: Matched ERM or the author online group-DRO achieves equal or better full-task tradeoff; lowering training F alone cannot establish transfer.
closest_alternative: Sagawa et al. group DRO and ordinary ERM. The entropic static dual and persistent online adversary are distinct algorithms, neither is new.
decisive_comparison: Compare same data/head/regularization/iterations and total group statistics cost; predeclare average and worst native task outcomes, preserve both adverse and favorable results.
legacy_code_audit: Legacy I11 correctly implements memoryless softmax group-loss weighting on ScienceQA/A-OKVQA; its groups are not the three evaluation-task groups.
review_limit: Conditional finite-dimensional conjugate/gradient reviewed; joint native evidence, parent failure and originality remain pending.
